elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 instead makes all programs and every writing or work of authorship created by M&I in performing the Services M&I's sole property.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment to Customer is included; Section 10.5 grants only a licence.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 17.2 provides that Customer has no rights in M&I-provided software, systems, documentation, procedures, and related materials except for the stated use rights.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 makes the Developed Software licence perpetual but does not extend that licence expressly to pre-existing or other Vendor IP embedded in it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The irrevocable licence applies to Developed Software, not expressly to Vendor IP embedded in the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The royalty-free licence applies to Developed Software, without expressly covering embedded Vendor IP.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 17.1 states that Customer remains the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 permits use for the broader 'purposes contemplated by this Agreement,' rather than limiting M&I to processing Customer Data solely to provide the Services.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The provisions allocate Developed Software solely to M&I and Customer Data solely and exclusively to Customer, with no joint ownership created.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 preserves M&I's sole ownership of its programs, including ideas, know-how, and concepts, and Section 17.2 preserves M&I's rights in its systems and related materials.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 grants Customer a perpetual licence to Developed Software, broadly defined as writings and works of authorship created in performing the Services.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly permits Customer to use and modify Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly permits Customer to sublicense Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 permits use for the broader 'purposes contemplated by this Agreement' and does not impose the required sole-purpose processing limitation.
